subject: Post-demo: cost calibration + program ask — Zenbyte next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Rao <samir@zenbyte.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 21:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: cost calibration + program ask — Zenbyte next steps

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great demo and helpful context on the GenAssist integration. Per our discussion, I pulled together a quick usage snapshot (attached) based on the call and the sample payloads you shared, plus an initial pricing worksheet with three options (pay-as-you-go, 12-month committed, 24-month ramp).

Quick recap of the things we need from you to firm up a formal offer: 
- A realistic monthly token run-rate for months 1, 3, and 6 (ballpark is fine).
- Targeted unit economics (what $/1M tokens would make this work for Zenbyte).
- Any procurement constraints (PO required, preferred DocuSign signatory, legal redlines).

As a reminder of program options we discussed:
- Startup program: one-time founder credit + 3 months reduced unit rate (qualification depends on stage & ARR).
- Committed-use: 12- or 24-month upfront/annualized discounts with volume bands and ramp profiles.
- Multi-year incentives: deeper discounts at the 2–3M token/month band with minimums and quarterly true-ups.

I attached the usage snapshot (zenbyte_usage_snapshot.pdf) and a first-pass pricing workbook. If you can reply with the three run-rate numbers and the target $/1M token metric, I will loop in Lauren for procurement and Ben for the formal pricing sheet (we can iterate to align on a 12-mo committed model + founder credit).

Proposed next step: 30-minute procurement & finance sync on Monday 7/5 to align on budget and sign-off path. Are you available 9–11am PT?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0122

Attachment: zenbyte_usage_snapshot.pdf, proposed-pricing-v2.xlsx

From: Samir Rao <samir@zenbyte.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Cc: Kelsey Monroe <kelsey@zenbyte.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost calibration + program ask — Zenbyte next steps

Jordan —

Really helpful summary, thanks. Quick answers below (happy to follow up in the sync):

Estimated token run-rate (requests are complex so these are conservative):
- Month 1 (pilot): ~75M tokens/month
- Month 3 (post-opt): ~350M tokens/month
- Month 6 (scale): ~1.4B tokens/month

Target unit economics: our finance/engineering target is ~$850 per 1M tokens (that keeps our GTM math intact). We understand top-tier discounts may be required to hit that; curious where Redwood stands on committed tiers vs. a pure payg price.

Procurement notes:
- PO is preferred for enterprise billing, but we can sign DocuSign to start.
- Legal will want SOC2 and data isolation notes (can you attach SOC2 summary and a short note on data residency?).
- If there's a founder/early-stage credit program that reduces T1 pricing for first 3 months, that helps our runway — please include details.

Kelsey: looping you in — high-level ask is to validate the ~$850/1M target and confirm path to a 12–24 month committed discount structure that preserves a price near that target at scale.

On the 7/5 sync — I can do 9:30–10:00am PT, Kelsey can do 10–11am PT. If 9:30 works for you, lock it and we will send calendar invite.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Head of Ops | Zenbyte
samir@zenbyte.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Rao <samir@zenbyte.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost calibration + program ask — Zenbyte next steps

Samir —

Appreciate the numbers and the clarity on target $/1M. Those run-rates map well to the volume bands we use for committed pricing. Quick notes from our side:

- Pay-as-you-go provides flexibility but your $850/1M target is aggressive for pure PAYG at the 1.4B/month scale; committed-use is where we can get you into that neighborhood.
- A 12-month committed plan with a ramp (75M -> 350M -> 1.4B) plus quarterly true-ups is the cleanest commercial path to align pricing and risk.
- Founder credit / startup program: we can offer a one-time $10k credit + 3 months of reduced T1 rate for qualifying early-stage companies. I'll confirm eligibility criteria with Growth.

I've attached an updated pricing workbook (proposed-pricing-v2.xlsx) with a model that targets three price points and shows blended $/1M based on your ramp. Ben, can you confirm whether the blended $/1M in tab "12m_ramp" can be tightened further if Zenbyte is willing to commit to a minimum quarterly true-up?

Lauren — can you prep a short procurement checklist (PO vs DocuSign flow, typical SLA exceptions, SOC2 link) for Samir and Kelsey? I'll include SOC2 summary now so legal has that in hand.

Samir — for the calendar, 9:30am PT on 7/5 works for me. Please send invite; we'll use that time to cover procurement, commercial, and a proposed timeline to sign.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-pricing-v2.xlsx, soc2-summary.pdf

From: Kelsey Monroe <kelsey@zenbyte.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>, Samir Rao <samir@zenbyte.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: cost calibration + program ask — Zenbyte next steps

Jordan / Samir,

Quick note from me: thanks for the clarity team. We want to move quickly on a 12-month committed structure that gives predictable unit economics while allowing us to ramp. The ask from my side: please surface a single-sheet commercial one-pager (total committed tokens, quarterly true-up mechanics, blended $/1M, founder credit applied) and a DocuSign-ready order form by end of day Wednesday 7/7. If we can see that, I'll unblock finance to start the PO.

Samir — let's also make sure legal has the SOC2 summary Ben/Jordan provided before the procurement meeting.

Kelsey Monroe
CEO | Zenbyte
